findings.summary: Linked product cards still don't lift on hover. The hovered card gets a pale fill on its text area only. It doesn't move -4px and gets no hard offset shadow, in light or dark, so it sits flush with the rest of the grid. The hard lift on linked cards is a signature element. This is unchanged since the previous round, even though the spec now has a 'Linked cards' paragraph and a verify step.
findings.promptFix: A linked card's hover is the lift. A fill change never replaces it. Put the .lift class (or its exact hover rule: translate -4px -4px plus shadow.md in color.shadow.hard) on the card's outermost bordered element, the one that receives the pointer. Any background tint is optional and only comes together with the lift. Put the card's hover in the Interaction table as 'Linked card | lift, as buttons'. In the final check, hover one card in each theme and confirm that its position and shadow changed. A color change alone fails the check.

findings.summary: The account-menu trigger is still solid pink while its menu is open, in light, dark and mobile. That makes a second loud pink element and breaks the one-pink-action rule. The spec bans a pink open-menu trigger, but its own ghost-button recipe ('.lift--ghost:hover fills pink') makes any ghost trigger turn pink while the pointer rests on it after the click. The Interaction table also has no open-trigger row.
findings.promptFix: Give every menu, popover, select and disclosure trigger an explicit open state, [aria-expanded="true"], that wins over hover: color.surface.raised fill with the ink border (or color.action.inverse for a solid trigger), no pink, at a selector specificity at least as high as the ghost hover rule. Add an 'Open trigger' row to the Interaction table. Exclude triggers from the ghost button's pink hover: a trigger's hover shows the ink border only. Verify by opening every menu with the pointer left on its trigger and checking that nothing pink appears besides the screen's one main action.

findings.summary: The spec contradicts itself on selected checkboxes and switches. The Interaction table says a color.action.primary (pink) fill, while Color use and the Checkbox and Switch sections say an ink fill, never pink. This run drew ink switches, but another run could follow the table.

In light mode, the loading 'Refreshing...' button on the color band uses the disabled style: gray label on a pale-gray fill with a hairline border. It looks washed out against the band. The spec's disabled recipe conflicts with its own 'no disabled-looking text on a band' rule, and its loading recipe (same button, coin in place of the label) wasn't used. Dark mode stays readable.

On product detail pages the header shows no current-page pill. 'Shop' is plain text even though the page sits under the shop's band and breadcrumb, while the home and cart screens fill their own section's pill.

Two small drawings break from the sticker language. The about page's heading mark is a solid stock speech-bubble icon rather than an outline icon or an ink-outlined sticker. The sweater sticker has short sleeves and almost the same outline as the t-shirt sticker, so two items read as one drawing in two colors.

notes: Review: 129/129 checklist items by 8 reviewer(s) and a lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.3/review-1).
Review: 129/129 checklist items by 8 reviewers and the lead reviewer (showcase/runs/hardlift/0.1.0-rc.3/review-1). I opened the card-hover and user-menu-open screenshots to confirm both majors.
No blockers. Nothing overlaps or gets cut off in a way that breaks a task, no text is unreadable, and the reference's identity holds.

Fixed since rc.2: every product tile and article figure is now its own sticker object or scene (11 different products, two different figures), which brings back the reference's colorful marketplace wall. The one-pink-action rule now holds for component-owned buttons (Refresh and Clear filters are ink). The product detail price is now a pink tag. The subscribe confirmation is no longer nested inside a raised card.

The four apps clearly look like one family. They share paper and ink, regular-weight display type, one full-width band per section with an ink rule under it, ink-filled current-page pills (paper-filled in dark), outlined cards, pink price tags and one pink main action. Dark mode maps the same way in every app.

Someone who knows the reference would recognize it: the yellow sticker hero with tilted coins and tags cropped at the band edge, and the flooded shop band with its pill strip over a dense, colorful sticker grid.

Signature elements: bands, outline pills and sticker art now hold across all apps. The hard lift shows on buttons and row actions but is still missing on linked cards, which is where the reference shows it most.

Two majors keep this candidate from passing, and both are carried over from rc.2: the card lift (the agent ignored the recipe, so the fix is to make it the required hover and check it) and the pink open-menu trigger (partly caused by the spec, because the ghost button's pink hover wins over the open state).
